races.name: Ray And Eileen Mclean Memorial EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Jw 4x4 Northallerton Irish EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Heineken 0% Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Hover On The Wind
runners_data.note: In sparkling 5f Good-ground form (two wins in last four on identical surface), but this horse is a genuine hold-up type who will be unable to settle as far back as preferred with this pace bias; style fit is compromised here (0.93), and Paul Mulgley's yard has a blank recent 14-day strike rate, though the form credentials remain strong if it can adapt.|
runners_data.comment: Hover On The Wind has back-to-back wins in his recent starts but tumbled to seventh last time out, and ranked eighth of nine on our figures he faces a stiff ask here; has run over today's trip and going, and 28 days off should have him fresh.

runners_data.name: Managing Director
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner meeting a direct rival in Equity Law for the lead; won on Good ground over 5f (1/5f/GOO) and is on a short 20-day turnaround, but trainer Geoff Oldroyd has a lean 14-day record (0/1) and the horse's soft-ground run was poor — Good ground is essential for this profile.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out suggests Managing Director is knocking on the door, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; carrying 128 lb from stall two, the main risk is whether that weight blunts his finishing effort when it matters most.

runners_data.name: Our Absent Friends
runners_data.note: Veteran 8-year-old prominent runner with a recent win on Good 5f ground (1/5f/GOO) and solid course familiarity; Shane Gray takes over and the trainer has run 6 in 14 days without a winner, but this horse's profile is straightforward and may benefit if the pace war plays into its hands.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of nine on our figures and officially rated just 69, Our Absent Friends is hard to fancy despite a win last time out; he has run over today's trip and going before, but five inconsistent efforts in his last six starts make that recent victory hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Winchurch
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner by natural style, but OR 78 and Tom Eaves aboard for a yard (Appleby) that has landed one from 22 in 14 days; recent form includes back-to-back 5f wins on Good and Soft, and at 16 days since last run should be fresh — his ability to track from midfield makes him one of the more interesting in this field.|
runners_data.comment: Winchurch has winning form in recent starts, with victories two, four, and six starts back, though he was unplaced last time out; he has run over today's trip and going, but a struggling trainer at just 5% recently gives cause for pause.

runners_data.name: Rock Of England
runners_data.note: Three wins from 15 similar-going runs and a consistent form string (131214) underline serious 5f Good-ground ability; a true hold-up runner placed into midfield by the race shape (STYLE_FIT 0.94), and Luke Morris rides for a Paul Midgley yard that has been quiet (0/17 over 14 days), but the horse's course-specific record is among the best here.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Rock Of England is hard to fancy at the weights despite a lively recent record that includes a win two starts back; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 13 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Equity Law
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner carrying headgear (hg:p) who is returning after 54 days off, and Tim Easterby's yard is firing (5/69 in 14 days); three wins and six places from 12 similar-going runs make Good turf over 5f the ideal conditions — the key question is whether the battle with Managing Director takes too much out of him.|
runners_data.comment: Equity Law won last time out and was second two starts back, giving him a fine run of recent form, though 54 days off the track and a burden of 130 lb from stall 8 are factors to weigh against him here.

runners_data.name: Moulin Booj
runners_data.note: Top-rated at OR 81, Daniel Tudhope is a major booking and the horse won last time (form finishes ...521) on Good 5f turf; 3 days since last run is very tight and the trainer (George Scott, 2/12 in 14 days) will need this to be a quick recovery, but the combination of class edge and jockey quality makes this one of the most dangerous profiles in the field.|
runners_data.comment: Moulin Booj arrives on the back of a win last time out and a second two starts back, giving him a sharp recent profile that marks him out as a leading threat, though the quick three-day turnaround is the obvious question mark over whether he can back it up at his best.

runners_data.name: Accrual
runners_data.note: Produced a win over 5f on Good ground (1/5f/GOO) but similar-going history is narrow (1/15 with only 1W1P), and a recent unfinished run (U in form) raises questions; William Pyle is a low-profile booking, Ruth Carr's yard is active (5/24 in 14 days), but the going-record concern is real and this horse may need things to fall perfectly.|
runners_data.comment: Accrual returns just 13 days after a winning effort, has run over today's trip and going, and his rating of 84 underlines his claims as a leading threat; the main risk is that fifth two starts back hints at inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Emerald Harmony
runners_data.note: Consistent 5f performer (1W6P in similar going across 11 runs) whose natural hold-up style is compromised by the redistribution in this field — it will be unable to drop out as far as preferred and the style fit (0.94) is fractionally reduced as a result; David Nolan is an experienced handler of this scenario, and Midgley's stable has been quiet, but the form string ending in a 6 is a mild concern.|
runners_data.comment: Emerald Harmony shaped with real promise when third two starts back and runner-up three starts back, and at 20 days since her last outing she arrives here in solid order, with experience of today's trip and going working in her favour from stall three.

races.paceDynamic: Equity Law and Managing Director are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead hard from the off over Thirsk's sharp, flat 5f, creating a genuinely contested gallop rather than a soft, uncontested lead. That honest tempo — set by two horses of similar intent — will stretch the field early and compress finishing margins, making a strong pace scenario the most probable race shape. The beneficiaries will be horses capable of sitting just off the speed in the first two furlongs and sustaining their effort through the short straight; a prominent-to-midfield tracking position is the sweet spot here, as pure hold-up horses will be giving away too much ground on a trip this short with this much pace. This field holds more hold-up types than can realistically operate from their natural position — Emerald Harmony, Rock Of England, and Hover On The Wind are all true hold-up runners who will be shuffled forward by the race shape, reducing their effectiveness; of the three, Rock Of England's consistent form figures give it the best chance of still competing, but none will secure their genuine preferred position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Equity Law and Managing Director burn each other off and the hold-up-tracking horses sweep past in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The two leaders press hard through the first two furlongs, setting a pace that brings the field into contention approaching the final furlong; horses who have covered the ground smoothly from a midfield-tracking position — not true hold-up types — benefit most here. Moulin Booj and Winchurch, both capable of sitting handy enough in this field and with strong recent 5f Good-ground form, are ideally profiled to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Equity Law or Managing Director gains a marginal lead and has enough in reserve to hold on as the field closes
scenarios.body: One of the two leaders breaks cleaner than the other, controls the gallop slightly more comfortably, and sustains their effort through Thirsk's flat straight, holding on as others fail to close in time. Equity Law's Good-ground record is excellent (3W6P in similar going) and carries headgear; if Managing Director is the one who blinks first, Equity Law could dictate and win.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace duel between Equity Law and Managing Director is severe enough to open the race up for true closers arriving late
scenarios.body: In this shape, the contested early fractions create a significant pace collapse near the line, and horses coming from off the pace mop up; however, this scenario is discounted because the majority of the hold-up horses — Hover On The Wind, Rock Of England, Emerald Harmony — are redistributed runners who will not be in their natural positions and are therefore less able to produce a true late burst. Moulin Booj, the highest-rated horse in the field (OR 81, ridden by Tudhope), has genuine hold-up credentials and recent wins on this exact surface and trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Tracks Through
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops at a genuinely strong gallop and a prominent-style runner off the pace of the leaders slots into position and outstays the field late
scenarios.body: Our Absent Friends, a prominent-style runner with a recent win on Good ground over 5f and proven course form, could benefit if the leaders empty and midfield runners are equally flattened; this is the least likely shape but not impossible given the age and course experience of an 8-year-old who has won in identical conditions. The probability is low because the prominent runners are not clearly superior in class and the scenario depends on a precise pace configuration.

watchPoints.text: Equity Law and Managing Director will lock horns for the lead from the off — watch how aggressively David Allan and P J McDonald commit in the first furlong, as the severity of that duel will define whether either can win or simply sets it up for others.

Moulin Booj, running just 3 days after its last start, must be monitored in the paddock and early in the race — if Daniel Tudhope is unusually restrained or the horse looks flat, the quick turnaround has taken its toll and its market position should be treated with caution.

Rock Of England, Hover On The Wind, and Emerald Harmony are all Paul Midgley runners whose natural hold-up style will be compromised by the pace dynamic — watch if any of them are forced wider or further forward than intended, as that redistribution will erode their chance significantly.

Winchurch's last recorded run was a 0 (unplaced/tailed off) in the most recent form figure — despite two previous wins on Good ground, watch for signs in the betting market or pre-race that trainer Michael Appleby's yard is expecting improvement rather than confirming current form.

Accrual's form contains an Unfinished (U) run recently — watch how William Pyle positions it in the early stages; if the horse shows any reluctance or sits detached at the rear, its narrow similar-going record (1/15) combined with the behavioural flag makes it easy to dismiss from winning calculations.

races.name: Andrew Seaton Celebration Cup Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Enchant
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced Burke filly (⚠ flag) whose only wins came at 6f on Good; steps up to 7f here with James Doyle and a 61-day break — the extra furlong and return from a rest make this a watch-it situation despite fair sim-going record.
runners_data.comment: Returned a winner two starts back but sixth last time out, and our figures put her well below the level required here; the 61-day absence adds further doubt, though she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Return Of The Gods
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's sole confirmed front runner who sets the tactical agenda for the whole field; won at this trip on Good last time and Tudhope knows him well, though the style-fit tag flags he may find prominent rivals harder to deal with if his position is challenged.
runners_data.comment: Winner two starts back and a close second three starts back, Return Of The Gods arrives fit on a 20-day break with experience over today's trip and the backing of a trainer firing at 31% in the past fortnight; the fourth last time out is a minor query, but his overall profile makes him the one to side with here.

runners_data.name: Zarvali
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's hold-up specialist with an excellent record over 7f on Good (1W3P from nine sim-going runs); only seven days since last run which keeps him fresh, and Oisin Orr is an astute jockey for a horse that needs cover before making a late move.

runners_data.name: Substance
runners_data.note: Mark Walford's hold-up type who has won at 8f and placed at 7f on Good, with headgear noted; 70-day absence is the main concern, though his class profile and stamina-based style suit a properly run seven.
runners_data.comment: Substance landed a win three starts back and franked that with a third last time out, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; the main risk is a 70-day absence returning fresh on 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Raging Raj
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent racer for Michael Herrington with a win and two places at this trip on Good; Tom Eaves navigating from second or third suits the expected pace shape, making him a natural dangers horse if Return Of The Gods does the work.
runners_data.comment: Raging Raj has the experience of today's trip and conditions in his favour, and a winner two starts back shows he can find the track, but a fifth last time out and 130 lb to carry are the checks on expectations here.

runners_data.name: Shadow Run
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon's runner has true hold-up instincts but is redistributed to midfield on the map — the field's density of rear-of-field types means Luke Morris will likely find his natural berth deeper than shown, extending the task on what is a horse whose best form came over 5-6f, shorter than this 7f trip.
runners_data.comment: Shadow Run has been placed twice in his last five starts — second last time out and a second four starts back — and he steps up with experience over today's trip and going under 127 lb, yet winless in recent starts remains the concern.

runners_data.name: Derrygarran Lad
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's lightly-raced sort (three runs, all placed) wearing headgear; Ryan Sexton takes the ride and the sim-going record is limited to one run at this trip on Good, so profile uncertainty is high despite the consistent placed form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts despite a pair of seconds and a third, Derrygarran Lad finds himself ranked bottom on our figures here, and with a speed rating of 64 he faces a stiff ask, though he has run over today's trip before and returns 26 days fresh.

runners_data.name: Indefensible
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears' prominent racer with the widest range of placed form at this trip on Good (1W4P from ten sim-going runs); Harry Russell rides for a trainer without a strike in 14 days, but Indefensible's consistency and proven 7f Good profile make it a live contender in the dominant scenario.
runners_data.comment: Indefensible won last time out and has run over today's distance and going before, giving him solid claims, though he has been third on two of his last three starts and our rating ranks him sixth of eight in this field.

races.paceDynamic: Return Of The Gods is the confirmed front runner here and, with no genuine challenger likely to force an early duel, Daniel Tudhope should be able to dictate a sensible, unchallenged gallop across Thirsk's flat seven furlongs. Raging Raj and Indefensible will press from prominent positions, giving the race a legitimate but not brutal tempo — enough to keep it honest without turning it into a sprint test. Shadow Run carries a redistribution flag: a genuine hold-up type pushed into the midfield map because the rear of the field is crowded; its true tactical position will be deeper than shown, meaning it faces a longer run than ideal. On Good ground at a fair pace with a single, uncontested pace-setter controlling affairs, the race shape strongly favours horses that can race prominently or in midfield and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs rather than closers dependent on a true end-to-end burn.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Return Of Gods Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Return Of The Gods jumps cleanly and settles into an uncontested lead at a controlled but honest gallop, the race unfolds on his terms throughout.
scenarios.body: Tudhope allows the favourite to stride clear from the front, and horses that can track closely and quicken with him — rather than those needing a fast pace to close into — are best positioned; a measured tempo over seven furlongs suits the prominent brigade who can conserve energy before striking.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Return Of The Gods is marginally outrun early and the pace proves just quick enough to expose him late, a horse tracking in second or third cruising can swoop.
scenarios.body: Raging Raj or Indefensible, both pressing from prominent positions, would be perfectly placed to capitalise as the leader tires in the final furlong; this scenario rewards horses with a strong finishing kick from a close-up position rather than a true front runner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Surge On Fast Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely quick and the field strings out, creating a true test of stamina through the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Zarvali and Substance, both Hold-Up types with 7f Good form, would have the most ground to make up but their profiles suit a truly run race where stamina outweighs position; Zarvali in particular has a solid record at this trip on Good ground and could pick up late ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Return Of The Gods is pressured unexpectedly from the outset, fracturing the pace into an uneven, stop-start affair that renders positional advantage irrelevant.
scenarios.body: An erratic tempo would scramble the field order and allow a hold-up type like Zarvali or Substance to emerge from an unexpected angle; however this scenario is unlikely given the absence of a genuine pace rival and the style-fit concerns around Shadow Run actually securing a true hold-up berth.

watchPoints.text: Return Of The Gods is the race-shaper — watch whether Tudhope gets a clean break and settles comfortably; if he is niggled at or pressured in the first two furlongs the entire pace dynamic changes.

Shadow Run's true running position will be deeper than the map indicates — watch how Luke Morris positions in the first furlong, as any wider berth or traffic issue in a compressed midfield could effectively end its chance before the race develops.

Enchant is lightly raced with a question mark over the 7f trip; watch early market moves and how James Doyle positions her — if she gets a prominent berth she could outrun her profile, but a wide draw or slow start on the return from 61 days is a real risk.
Zarvali runs only seven days after its last start — watch paddock demeanour and early settle for signs of freshness or fatigue, as Fell horses returning quickly can run flat if not right.

Derrygarran Lad's three-run sample makes it genuinely hard to profile; watch whether Ryan Sexton rides him forward or holds back, as either style change from such a lightly-raced runner could signal trainer intention.

races.name: Malton Marquees Racing Through The Summer Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Roaring Ralph
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in strong form (1-1-3 in last five starts including two wins over today's 8f on Good), Dods stable in reasonable nick, blinkers likely to keep him focused — must secure a forward berth early to be effective.
runners_data.comment: Roaring Ralph has won three times in his last six starts, but he has a bit to find on our figures, ranked 11 of 15, and an unplaced effort last time out does little to inspire confidence, even if he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Style Of Life
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner returning from 91 days off under PJ McDonald; has won over this course and distance on Good ground and can exploit any lack of pressure, though the layoff introduces doubt over his freshness over a full mile.

runners_data.name: Bloodsweatandtyres
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with only one run on Good turf in recent history (0 wins, 0 places in similar going), better form on Tapeta; Ben Robinson will try to push forward but this surface is a legitimate concern against sharper rivals.
runners_data.comment: Bloodsweatandtyres has experience of today's distance and going, and a win four starts back gives him a recent winning benchmark; at 134 lb from stall 10, the weight burden after three below-par efforts since that victory is the concern.

runners_data.name: Military Leader
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type with four places from five runs over 8f on Good, including a recent win; only 6 days since last run which needs monitoring, but Paul Mulrennan and the Makin yard are both in form and he gets his ideal position easily here.
runners_data.comment: Military Leader has placed in each of his last four starts, including two wins in his last six, and has run over today's trip and going — a consistent profile. However, six days between runs is a quick turnaround, and 133 lb is a stern burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Alessia Fernanda
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has shown she stays the mile well and her best form is on Good turf (2nd latest start); Zak Wheatley rides and she needs a clean gap to appear late, which depends entirely on the size of the field breaking apart.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out after a mid-table spell, Alessia Fernanda brings distance and going experience and rates 3 lb above her official mark, yet her record in recent starts shows inconsistency, and 132 lb from stall nine will test her here.

runners_data.name: Harswell Ruby
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid claims over this course and distance, four places from last five runs on Good — Roger Fell stable hit T14:1/15 — but she has not beaten rivals of this quality yet and must cope with traffic ahead of her.
runners_data.comment: Harswell Ruby arrives in decent nick on a 16-day turnaround, and her second three starts back gives her a strong claims against this field; drawing stall one and carrying 132 lb while yet to win in recent starts is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Donna Nook
runners_data.note: Prominent type who won over 8f on Good and has been placed four times in his last five; David O'Meara sends him out sharp (T14:9/53 is strongest trainer stat in the field), visor worn, and Tudhope is a significant booking at Thirsk.
runners_data.comment: Donna Nook catches the eye on our ratings as the second-ranked runner in this field, and she has experience of both today's trip and going to call on, stepping back up having won four starts back. The worry is that three subsequent fourths suggest she may struggle to convert.

runners_data.name: Green Pursuit
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse stepping back up from 7f and returning after 61-day break; best form is on Good but top-speed figures are modest and Seb Spencer is a small operation — needs everything to fall right from an off-pace position.
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back represents Green Pursuit's best recent showing, and he has run over today's trip and going, giving him necessary experience heading in; yet to score in his last five starts, though our rating of 84 marks him the one to beat from stall 12 fresh off a 61-day absence.

runners_data.name: Jesmond Dawn
runners_data.note: Prominent-to-midfield runner with excellent recent form including a win and two places over 8f on Good; Grant Tuer is small but hit T14:1/6, Oliver Stammers rides, and this horse has a clean profile for a race where traffic opens.
runners_data.comment: Jesmond Dawn ranks 12th of 15 on our figures, making him hard to fancy, and he finished fifth last time out; the win came two starts back. He has run over today's trip and going, and draws stall two carrying 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Up The Jazz
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who has won over this trip on Good, placed five times in similar going — very consistent profile — 5lb claimer Ethan Tindall takes the ride, which trims the raw ability but the horse's natural finishing run is genuine.
runners_data.comment: Up The Jazz showed well when winning three starts back and was a close second two starts ago, but seventh last time out clouds his claims; he has run over today's distance and going before, and 20 days since that below-par effort leaves him needing to bounce back from stall four off 129 lb.

runners_data.name: Degale
runners_data.note: True hold-up type with 10 runs at this trip on Good ground and a solid record of placing; pattern of finishing third to fifth rather than winning suggests a modest ceiling in a competitive 15-runner handicap at this mark.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Degale does at least bring distance and going experience to this assignment and steps in here on a fresh 15-day break, though carrying 127 lb from stall six and ranking tenth of fifteen on ratings suggests he faces a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Mount King
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse — best form is a win and three places over 8f on Good (10/15 in similar going) — but with four redistributed types ahead of him in the map he is unlikely to get his natural rearward position and races partly out of role today; Tim Easterby T14:5/69 is a high-volume yard with good strike rate.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 14 of 15 on our figures, Mount King makes it hard to build a case despite a second last time out and a winner two starts back; he has run over today's trip and going, but at 125 lb from stall seven, better efforts look needed to trouble these rivals.

runners_data.name: Travis
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse with a sequence of thirds and a win over 7f on Good, consistent but not explosive; the field's depth of similar types means he is unlikely to get as far back as he needs, and Geoffrey Harker's T14:0/3 offers no recent encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Travis has placed third in three consecutive starts and was a winner four starts back, but two unplaced efforts in his last six suggest inconsistency holds him back; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 122 lb from stall 8, and returns on a sharp 14-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Palmarian
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr runner with headgear (hood) and a win and second over 8f on Good — genuinely effective at this trip — but as one of four hold-up types crowded out of their natural position, he'll need to be more forceful than usual to get competitive ground.
runners_data.comment: Palmarian has won once in his last six starts, with a second two starts back offset by a string of poor efforts either side, and ranked 13 of 15 on our figures he faces a stiff ask here; has run over today's trip and going, and 22 days between runs suggests he arrives reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Miss Willows
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up mare returning after 59 days off; best form at 7f, Simon Whitaker yard at T14:0/6, and with four hold-up rivals competing for the same late space she faces a compounded task to get a clear run in a 15-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Miss Willows won one in her last five starts but has been unplaced in two of the three since, and ranked last of 15 on our figures she faces a stiff task; a runner-up last time out and experience of today's trip and going are the only crumbs of comfort.

races.paceDynamic: Style Of Life is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with 91 days off the track, will need to be ridden positively by PJ McDonald to dominate — a sustainable, unhurried gallop on Good ground over a mile at Thirsk is the likely result. Behind him, Roaring Ralph, Bloodsweatandtyres, Military Leader, Harswell Ruby and Donna Nook all want prominent positions, creating a congested battle for the first two or three berths between furlongs 6 and 5, which risks a ragged, uneven tempo through the middle of the race. That prominent congestion means horses tracking in fourth to sixth — sitting just off the scrimmage — are best placed to pounce when the pace quickens turning for home, without having been trapped in a shuffle. This shape most clearly favours genuine prominent-to-midfield closers who can sit third to sixth early and deliver a sustained run through the final two furlongs; the field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear, and Mount King, Travis, Palmarian and Miss Willows are unlikely to secure their natural position — those most likely to grab a genuine prominent berth ahead of them are Military Leader, Roaring Ralph and Donna Nook.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Clean Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If Style Of Life dictates a fair but uncontested gallop and prominent rivals find positions without incident.
scenarios.body: Style Of Life sets a regulated tempo and those who track him closely in second to fourth are gifted a perfect tow into the straight; the horses who travel prominently without scrimmaging get first run and hold on as the closer types can't get through.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage, Midfielder Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the six prominent-wanting runners battle for position and create a ragged, slightly hot pace through the middle of the race.
scenarios.body: The congestion burns off the front movers and leaves an opening for a horse sitting just off the melee in fifth or sixth who travels sweetly before unleashing a clean run through the final furlong; this suits the honest, consistent types with good mileage form on Good ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Hold-Up Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Style Of Life is harried early, sets too slow a crawl, or drops out, and closers come with a late sweeping run.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow race compresses the field and rewards the horse with the sharpest turn of foot launched from off the pace in the final two furlongs; however, several supposed hold-up types here are redistributed from prominent roles, so the true closer advantage is narrower than it first appears.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Sticks, Pace Flatters
scenarios.trigger: If Style Of Life is simply allowed to coast on a very easy lead and the chasing pack fail to coordinate a challenge.
scenarios.body: An untroubled solo lead on Good ground over a flat mile can be unassailable when the field is fractured and prominent rivals have spent energy scrapping; the front-runner holds on as closers run out of real estate.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion — Roaring Ralph, Bloodsweatandtyres, Military Leader, Harswell Ruby and Donna Nook all want the same positions behind Style Of Life; watch for bumping and shuffling between furlongs 7 and 5 that could stop a prominent racer cold.
Style Of Life's 91-day absence is the biggest pace variable — if he is flat or gets harried, the entire pace map dissolves and a very different race shape unfolds around the final quarter-mile.

Mount King, Travis, Palmarian and Miss Willows are true hold-up horses forced into midfield by field congestion; if any of them try to push forward to reclaim their natural ground they risk running too freely and dying in the straight.

Donna Nook with Daniel Tudhope is the most significant jockey-trainer combination in the prominent group (O'Meara T14:9/53) — watch his early positioning closely as Tudhope will know exactly where to place him to exploit the traffic.

Good ground is confirmed all day at Thirsk and has held consistent; no surface surprise expected, but horses with proven Good form (Military Leader, Roaring Ralph, Jesmond Dawn, Up The Jazz) all carry a small edge over those with shorter similar-going records.

races.name: Birra Moretti Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Prince Achille
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old hold-up performer for Jedd O'Keeffe returning after a 148-day absence, whose best recent form (four placed efforts at 10f-11f on Soft/Standard) suggests he stays this trip but has yet to win on Good ground in the last five runs; the long layoff is the key query.|
runners_data.comment: Prince Achille rates ahead of his rivals on our figures and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a live threat despite carrying 136 lb; the concern is he is winless in his last five starts and returns after 148 days off.

runners_data.name: Halimede
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's three-year-old arrives in sharp form with back-to-back wins at 12f-13f, the latest just six days ago, and despite her true running style being that of a hold-up horse she is effectively the only plausible pace-setter here and is mapped to the front accordingly — her notable tendency to fade late is the main risk to that lead.|
runners_data.comment: Halimede arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and, with only six days between runs, fitness is not in question; she has run over today's trip and her overall profile makes her our pick despite carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Recobella
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's five-year-old arrives four days after her last run with good recent form including a win on Good ground at 10f, but as a genuine hold-up type she is shown in midfield only because there is insufficient room at the rear — her true style is to come from off the pace, which in a race Halimede controls from the front may mean she simply has too much to do.|
runners_data.comment: Recobella ran a fine second last time out and was a winner two starts back, showing she retains form, and her experience over today's trip and going underlines her claims; the main risk is the quick four-day turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Halimede is the only confirmed pace-setter in this three-runner field, and with just two rivals to contend with, she is almost certain to bowl along in front unchallenged at a sustainable, controlled gallop over this 1m4f trip on Good turf. Prince Achille and Recobella are both genuine hold-up types, meaning the race effectively splits into a lone leader against two closers who must produce their effort from off the pace. A single-pace, uncontested lead at Thirsk over this distance on Good ground suits a stayer who can dictate and conserve energy, making it very difficult for hold-up horses to generate the momentum needed to haul back a relaxed front-runner. This race shape strongly favours the prominent/lead profile — specifically Halimede, who is dictating her own race — and closers will need a tactical mishap or a genuine stamina test to peg her back. Note that the field contains more genuine hold-up types than can naturally vary their position: Recobella, mapped to midfield, is in truth a hold-up horse and is unlikely to naturally secure a prominent berth.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Halimede Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Halimede bowls along from the front at a controlled pace and neither closer can generate a decisive late run.
scenarios.body: Halimede sets a comfortable, uncontested gallop, conserves energy through the middle stages, and kicks clear from the home turn before Prince Achille or Recobella can wind up their challenges; her two recent wins at 12f-13f on Good-to-Standard ground confirm she stays and quickens. Hold-up horses face too much ground to make up against a fresh leader who has dictated every yard.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Her Down
scenarios.trigger: If Halimede goes too fast early or ties up late, allowing one of the hold-up horses to reel her in on the run-in.
scenarios.body: Halimede's tendency to fade in the finish — flagged in her profile — could be exploited if she has gone a fraction quick in the early stages on this flat track, opening the door for a sustained late challenge; Prince Achille, who has placed multiple times at this trip on similar going, is the most likely beneficiary given his consistent placed form at 10f-11f. Recobella's Good-ground win at 10f and two further placed efforts at 12f give her credentials here if she can close the gap from her mapped midfield berth.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Recobella Makes Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Recobella's recent win on Good ground (1f ago) translates to a sharp finishing burst that catches Halimede and Prince Achille.
scenarios.body: Recobella showed she can win on Good ground at 10f and has strong recent placing form, and if the pace has been sufficient to stretch the field she could arrive late with a decisive run; however, as a true hold-up type mapped to midfield, she is not guaranteed her natural position and this scenario depends on a genuine pace-test she may not get. Her rider's 5lb claim could offset any positional disadvantage if the race develops into a staying test.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy, Tactical Crawl
scenarios.trigger: If Halimede is restrained unexpectedly and all three horses dawdle, producing a sprint-finish over 1m4f.
scenarios.body: A very slow pace would theoretically suit the freshest horse or the one with the sharpest turn-of-foot, and in a three-runner crawl any of the trio could be competitive; however, this outcome is unlikely given Halimede's front-running profile and Sir Mark Prescott's tactical record of deploying horses purposefully. The scenario is given low weight because it runs entirely against the expected race shape.

watchPoints.text: Halimede's flagged tendency to fade in the finish is the single biggest risk in the race — watch whether she builds a big enough lead at the home turn to withstand the closers' runs.
Prince Achille returns after 148 days off the track; monitor his pre-race condition and whether he moves freely to post, as ring-rustiness over this trip could blunt his late effort.
Recobella runs just four days after her last start — watch the market for any sign of market support that would suggest connections believe the quick turnaround is not a concern.

With only three runners on Good ground at Thirsk, track position through the final bend will be crucial — watch which jockey takes the inside rail on the home turn, as it could prove decisive at this distance.
